required_changes_injected: CRITERION 2 VIOLATION — Champion carry-forward regression without documented reason. Prior cumulative state scored Champion at 4/10 with evidence 'James identified as engaged contact providing pricing and technical information.' Current analysis downgrades to 2/10 with a lengthy reconciliation that redefines 'champion' retroactively. The analysis argues the prior 4/10 'reflected engagement, not championing' and claims 'per the scoring rubric, a contact who is engaged and responsive but owns no confirmed internal next step scores 1–2/10.' This is a post-hoc reinterpretation of the rubric, not a carry-forward consistency check. If the prior assessment was incorrect, that must be stated explicitly as a correction to the cumulative state, not as a reframing of what the rubric means. The current analysis does identify one new concrete action (James sent a survey to the product team on August 7), which could justify maintaining or slightly adjusting the prior score, but the downgrade from 4/10 to 2/10 is presented as a 'reconciliation' rather than as a response to new information that contradicts the prior assessment. CRITERION 4 VIOLATION — Champion next steps use vague language. Step 1 asks 'When you brought this to your product and engineering leads, what was their reaction?' This is an open-ended discovery question, not a specific action with a concrete deliverable. Step 2 offers 'Would it help if we put together a one-page summary...' which is exploratory, not a committed action. Both lack the specificity required: 'Ask James to schedule a call with [executive name] by [date] to review pricing and technical fit' or '[contact TBD]: Confirm by August 14 whether the product team survey has been returned and executive pricing review is complete.' CRITERION 1 VIOLATION — Economic Buyer evidence quality. The analysis states 'no name, title, or direct engagement has been documented' and references only 'executive sign-off' as evidence. This is insufficient to support a 3/10 score. A 3/10 should include at least a paraphrase or quote indicating budget authority exists somewhere in the organization. The current evidence is too vague. Either lower the score to 1/10 (unknown) or provide a direct quote from the calls confirming executive involvement.
